title: Rapid Antibody Glycoengineering in Chinese Hamster Ovary Cells
protocol: Use Safari, Firefox, or Microsoft Edge to access the IDT website.
Select the Products and Services tab followed by RNA interference.
Select Design tool followed by the Generate Custom DsiRNA tab.
Enter the Fut8 Accession Number or manually enter the gene sequence to begin.
Obtain proposed Fut8 sequences from https://chogenome.org for both "CHO-K1" and "Chinese Hamster".
Perform a Manual BLAST search as the CHO cell genome is not available as a reference genome on the IDT website.
Click Search to generate DsiRNA sequences.
Assess the specificity of each DsiRNA using the Manual BLAST function with tax id:10029 (CHO cell lines and Chinese hamster).
Query coverage results indicate DsiRNA constructs match Fut8 at 100%, whilst complementarity against unintended targets is ≤76%.
Check that the DsiRNA specifically targets Fut8.
Ensure the GC content of the DsiRNA is between 30%-50%.
Select three DsiRNA targeting different locations of the Fut8 gene.
Purchase a predesigned non-targeting or scrambled DsiRNA for control experiments.
Centrifuge the DsiRNA at 13,300 x g for 1 min to pellet before opening the tube.
Reconstitute each lyophilized DsiRNA in nuclease-free duplex buffer to a 100 μM stock solution.
Incubate the stock solutions at room temperature for 30 min while shaking gently on an orbital shaker (50 rpm, 16 mm orbit).
Create a master mix by combining 20 μL of each DsiRNA construct targeting Fut8.
Prepare aliquots of the master mix and store at −20 °C.
Defrost a vial of cells for 2-3 min in a water bath set to 37 °C.
Clean the vial exterior with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube containing 9 mL of prewarmed medium appropriate for the cell line of choice.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 100 x g for 5 min.
Carefully remove and discard the medium without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of prewarmed medium.
Take an aliquot for counting.
Stain cells with Trypan blue if using a hemocytometer, or use an appropriate stain to distinguish live/dead cells when using an automated counter.
Transfer an appropriate volume of cell suspension to a 125 mL Erlenmeyer shake flask at a viable cell density of 3 x 10^5 cells/mL in 30 mL of medium (with optional supplementation of 50 μM MSX).
Place the flask with cells in an incubator set to 36.5 °C and 5% CO2.
Shake the flask at 150 rpm on a shaking platform with a 16 mm orbit.
Passage cells every 3-4 days at a seeding density of 2 x 10^5 cells/mL in a working volume of 50 mL in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer shake flask.
If using MSX, discontinue supplementation after the first passage.
Assess cell density and ensure viability is greater than 90% before each passage.
Clean the biosafety cabinet and all equipment with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Use an RNase inhibitor solution to avoid contamination.
Pellet cells at 100 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend pelleted cells in prewarmed medium to a density of 5 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer 8 μL of DsiRNA master mix or control to an electroporation cuvette.
Add 800 μL of cell suspension (4 x 10^6 cells) to the cuvette containing DsiRNA.
Mix both components thoroughly in the cuvette.
Apply a pulse condition of 1200 V, 0.1 ms, square waveform for electroporation.
Transfer the cell suspension from the cuvette to one well of a 6-well plate carefully.
Incubate cells without shaking at 36.5 °C and 5% CO2 for 10 min.
Add 800 μL of prewarmed media to each well, making a final volume of 1.6 mL per well.
Return the transfected cells to the incubator with conditions of 36.5 °C, 5% CO2 and shaking at 150 rpm (16 mm orbit).
Harvest supernatants and cells at 48 h post-transfection.
Measure IgG concentration using biolayer interferometry or another method of choice.
Hydrate protein A biosensor tips in sample diluent for 10-30 min.
Transfer cell suspensions into 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Pellet cells at 100 x g for 5 min.
Remove cells by filtration through a 0.45 µm nitrocellulose filter.
Carefully transfer the isolated supernatant containing IgG into a clean centrifuge tube without disturbing the pellet.
Use shaker speed of 2200 rpm and run time of 60 s for biolayer interferometry measurements.
Create a standard curve using an IgG standard (4 μL of each concentration).
Quantitate sample concentrations by loading 4 μL of the cell supernatant.
Clean the apparatus with lint-free wipes between each sample.
Link the standard curve to the unknown samples to interpolate the binding rate of the unknown samples.
Save the data and export as a csv or PDF file.
Prepare elution buffer containing 0.2 M glycine (pH 2.5) and sterilize by passing through a 0.22 μm filter.
Filter 1 mL of the isolated supernatant at room temperature using 0.22 μm microcentrifuge filter tubes until the entire supernatant flows through.
Pellet 150-200 μL of protein A agarose beads in 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes at 100 x g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Wash the protein A beads with 150-200 μL of cell culture medium.
Repeat centrifugation after washing the protein A beads.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend equilibrated protein A beads with 1 mL of supernatants from Step 3.2.3.
Load the resuspended beads into a 1 mL polypropylene tube.
Affix the tube to a rotary mixer and spin at 30 rpm for 60-90 min at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Collect the flow-through after incubation is complete.
Wash the beads with 1 mL of 1x PBS to remove unbound proteins.
Collect the wash fraction as well.
Elute IgG from the protein A beads by adding 3 mL of elution buffer to the polypropylene column.
Collect sequential fractions that drain from the column (500 μL each) into labeled tubes.
Neutralize the elution buffer with 25 μL of 1 M Tris pH 9.5 if the purified antibody is to be stored.
Exchange IgG elution buffer with 1x PBS.
Use the first elution fraction for downstream processing.
Keep all other fractions should they be required in the future.
Load elution A onto a 3 kDa molecular weight cutoff centrifugal concentrator.
Centrifuge at 13,300 x g for 40-50 min at 4 °C.
Discard the flow-through and add 500 μL of prechilled (4 °C) 1x PBS to dilute the residual supernatant.
Centrifuge the sample again using the same conditions until 50 μL of residual supernatant remains.
Add 500 μL of prechilled (4 °C) 1x PBS to dilute the residual supernatant and repeat the centrifugation process to obtain a 100x dilution of the supernatant.
Concentrate the supernatant to a final concentration of ~2.5 g·L-1 in 40 μL or less.
Transfer 200 μL of the magnetic bead solution to a 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Place the PCR tube onto the magnetic stand to separate the beads from the supernatant.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Place the tubes on a magnetic stand to separate contents.
Add purified protein sample to the tube and vortex.
Add denaturation buffer to the sample and incubate at 60 °C for 8 minutes with open lids.
Add PNGase F (500 units per sample) and incubate at 60 °C for 20 minutes with open lids.
Close the sample tube after PNGase F incubation and vortex.
Add acetonitrile to the sample, vortex, and incubate at room temperature for 1 minute.
Place the sample tubes in a magnetic stand to separate beads from solution.
Pipette out the supernatant carefully without touching the beads.
In a fume hood, add glycan labeling solution with a fluorophore to the sample.
Vortex the mixture well and incubate at 60 °C for 20 minutes with open lids.
Wash the sample three times in acetonitrile to remove excess dye.
Elute labeled glycans using DDI water.
Place the sample tube on a magnetic stand to separate beads from supernatant containing purified and labeled glycans.
Prepare glucose ladder standard, bracketing standards, and samples for analysis.
Load prepared materials into designated tray positions.
Run glycan analysis protocol.
Use software to analyze and identify glycans in the sample.
Quantify knockdown efficiency using western blot analysis with an anti-α-1,6-fucosyltransferase antibody.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter at 48 h post transfection.
Determine the volume of cell suspension equivalent to 5 x 10^6 cells for each experimental condition.
Transfer the appropriate volume of cell suspension from each condition to a sterile 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Pellet the cells at 13,200 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Lysate the cells with 200 μL of lysis buffer containing 1% v/v protease inhibitor cocktail at room temperature for 10 min.
Centrifuge the lysate at 13,200 x g for 10 min to remove cellular debris.
Transfer the cleared lysate to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Measure the protein concentration of each lysate using a spectrophotometer at 280 nm.
Adjust aliquots of each sample to have the same protein concentration.
Denature the protein samples by incubation at 100 °C for 10-15 min in DTT-SDS sample loading dye.
Load 15 μL of denatured samples and 5 μL of prestained protein ladder into an SDS-PAGE gel with a 12.5% resolving gel.
Run the samples at 25 mA per gel for 90 min or until the dye front reaches the end of the gel.
Carefully remove the gel from the cassette and incubate in 1x transfer buffer containing methanol.
Activate a PVDF membrane with methanol.
Assemble the gel and PVDF membrane for wet transfer.
Place an ice block in the transfer tank.
Submerge the entire transfer tank in ice to ensure cold conditions.
Run at 350 mA/100 V for 60 min.
Incubate the membrane in a blocking solution for 30 min at room temperature while shaking gently on an orbital shaker at 50 rpm (16 mm orbit).
Rinse the membrane with sterile water for 5 min and repeat.
Carefully cut the membrane horizontally at ~50 kDa using a clean scalpel guided by the visible protein ladder.
Incubate the membrane harboring proteins greater than 50 kDa with anti-α-1,6-fucosyltransferase antibody at 1:1000 in an antibody diluent buffer for 1 hour or overnight at 4°C.
Incubate the membrane with immobilized proteins less than 50 kDa with anti-GAPDH at 1:10,000 in diluent buffer for 1 hour or overnight at 4°C.
Wash the membranes for 5 min (x3).
Incubate the membranes with an appropriate secondary antibody for at least 30 min at room temperature.
Perform 3x washes with a wash buffer for 5 min.
Perform 3x washes with water.
Develop the membrane with a chromogenic substrate until bands appear (1-60 min).
Rinse the membrane 2x with water.
Allow the membrane to dry.
Capture an image of the membrane.
Perform densitometric analysis.
Calculate the ratio of the GAPDH signal in samples for normalization.
Divide the FUT8 signal intensity by the normalization factor for each lane.
Obtain the relative FUT8 protein expression.
